cards.title: Bioanalytical Method Validation Scope and Elements
cards.claim: Full validation is required for bioanalytical methods quantifying analytes in clinical and nonclinical studies. For chromatographic methods, this includes selectivity, specificity, matrix effect, calibration curve/range (LLOQ to ULOQ), accuracy, precision, carry-over, dilution integrity, stability, and reinjection reproducibility. For LBAs, it includes specificity, selectivity, calibration curve/range, accuracy, precision, carry-over, dilution linearity, and stability.
conditions: Applicable to establishing new methods or repurposing commercial kits/literature methods.
Applies to both chemical and biological drugs.
required_inputs: Blank matrix samples from multiple sources/lots.
limitations: Abstract-only material supports only what appears in the abstract.
Does not validate specific experimental data, only the method framework.
cards.downstream_use: Defines the quality control framework for any PK data used in EDA or modeling. Determines if concentration data is fit for purpose.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
